sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: The night of December 8th, 2013, a huge crowd appeared on a tree-lined boulevard in downtown Kiev, the capital of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 2013年12月8日晚，乌克兰首都基辅市中心的一条林荫大道上，聚集了大量人群。

sentences.en: The crowd was there to watch as a statue in the boulevard was pulled down by a crane.
sentences.zh: 人群聚集在那里，观看一台起重机将大道上的一座雕像拉倒。

sentences.en: That's producer Julia Barton.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人朱莉娅·巴顿。

sentences.en: It's a pretty large statue, a little more than 11 feet tall.
sentences.zh: 那是一座相当大的雕像，高约11英尺多。

sentences.en: And as it topples to the ground, the crowd goes wild.
sentences.zh: 当它轰然倒地时，人群沸腾了。

sentences.en: The toppled statue was of Vladimir Lenin, the communist leader who started the revolution that created the Soviet Union, of which Ukraine was once a part.
sentences.zh: 被推倒的雕像是弗拉基米尔·列宁，他是发动革命并创建苏联的共产主义领导人，而乌克兰曾是苏联的一部分。

sentences.en: The sculpture had shown Lenin striding into a breezy future, one that just barely rippled his marble suit coat.
sentences.zh: 雕塑中的列宁大步流星地迈向充满微风的未来，那微风甚至没能让他的大理石西装外套泛起多少涟漪。

sentences.en: But on the night of December 8th, 2013, this Lenin was no longer striding into a breezy future.
sentences.zh: 但在2013年12月8日那个夜晚，这位列宁不再迈向充满微风的未来了。

sentences.en: He was lying on the cold concrete as protesters continued to abuse him.
sentences.zh: 他躺在冰冷的混凝土上，抗议者们继续对他进行破坏。

sentences.en: They were just shouting that, you know, that this monument needed to be ruined.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在大喊，你知道的，这座纪念碑必须被毁掉。

sentences.en: And that he's a killer.
sentences.zh: 还说他是个杀人犯。

sentences.en: And that it's not the place for Soviet shit here anymore.
sentences.zh: 还说这里不再是苏联垃圾的容身之地了。

sentences.en: And Ukrainians are owners of this land.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人才是这片土地的主人。

sentences.en: Ukrainian photojournalist Alexander Tichensky rushed to the scene that night.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰摄影记者亚历山大·蒂琴斯基当晚赶到了现场。

sentences.en: He and his colleagues kept their cameras steady as the drama unfolded around them.
sentences.zh: 当周围上演这一幕时，他和同事们稳稳地架着摄像机。

sentences.en: Their footage ended up in a documentary they later made called All Things Ablaze.
sentences.zh: 他们的素材最终被剪辑进了一部名为《烈火万物》的纪录片中。

sentences.en: It shows people taking sledgehammers to Lenin's torso.
sentences.zh: 片中显示人们用大锤猛砸列宁的躯干。

sentences.en: The camera lingers on one man in a shiny tracksuit who spits on his hand, crosses himself three times, and starts whacking away with all of his might.
sentences.zh: 镜头停留在一个穿着闪亮运动服的男人身上，他往手上吐了口唾沫，在胸前画了三次十字，然后用尽全力猛砸。

sentences.en: But at some point, a thin old guy in a black coat emerges from the crowd and just wraps himself around Lenin's cheSt.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，一个穿着黑大衣的瘦弱老头从人群中钻了出来，紧紧抱住了列宁的胸部。

sentences.en: Yeah, he was trying to protect Lenin with his own body.
sentences.zh: 是的，他试图用自己的身体保护列宁。

sentences.en: And did he say anything this whole time?
sentences.zh: 他全程说了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, he was saying that it's not right, it's not correct.
sentences.zh: 是的，他说这样做是不对的，是不正确的。

sentences.en: Please don't do that.
sentences.zh: 请不要这样做。

sentences.en: It's, uh, barbarism.
sentences.zh: 这，呃，是野蛮行径。

sentences.en: Barbarism.
sentences.zh: 野蛮行径。

sentences.en: Barbarism, yeah.
sentences.zh: 野蛮行径，没错。

sentences.en: Another man pats the old communist on the back, a little threateningly.
sentences.zh: 另一个人拍了拍这位老共产党员的背，带着一点威胁的意味。

sentences.en: He's saying to this old communist sympathizer, you're the last one in the whole city, in the whole country, understand?
sentences.zh: 他在对这位老共产主义同情者说：你是整个城市、整个国家里的最后一个了，明白吗？

sentences.en: When you die, things in this country will get better.
sentences.zh: 等你死了，这个国家的情况就会好转。

sentences.en: Eventually, some volunteers in reflective vests lead the old man away by the arMs.
sentences.zh: 最终，几名穿着反光背心的志愿者架着老人的胳膊把他带走了。

sentences.en: His hat is gone.
sentences.zh: 他的帽子不见了。

sentences.en: He looks ready to faint.
sentences.zh: 他看起来快要晕倒了。

sentences.en: For the protesters, this old man and this statue of Lenin represent old Ukraine, one that is associated with the Soviet Union and with Russia.
sentences.zh: 对于抗议者来说，这位老人和这座列宁雕像代表着旧乌克兰，一个与苏联和俄罗斯联系在一起的乌克兰。

sentences.en: The protesters saw themselves as new Ukraine, independent and allied with the European Union.
sentences.zh: 抗议者们将自己视为新乌克兰，一个独立的、与欧盟结盟的乌克兰。

sentences.en: The same protests that brought down that Lenin statue eventually brought about a new government in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 正是那场推倒列宁雕像的抗议活动，最终促成了乌克兰新政府的诞生。

sentences.en: And that new government has been trying to get rid of all kinds of physical reminders of communism and of Russia.
sentences.zh: 而那个新政府一直试图清除各种关于共产主义和俄罗斯的物质印记。

sentences.en: Lenin statues, names of streets and towns.
sentences.zh: 列宁雕像、街道和城镇的名称。

sentences.en: But it hasn't always been easy to get rid of these things, logistically or politically, because it erases a part of history that is still important to some Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 但要清除这些东西并不总是那么容易，无论是在后勤上还是政治上，因为这抹去了一段对一些乌克兰人来说仍然很重要的历史。

sentences.en: People in different parts of Ukraine can see that history difference.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰不同地区的人们对这段历史有着不同的看法。

sentences.en: That's Katarina Dronova.
sentences.zh: 那是卡塔琳娜·德罗诺娃。

sentences.en: She's the legal editor at VoxUkraine.org, a website for Ukrainian news and policy analysis.
sentences.zh: 她是VoxUkraine.org的法律编辑，这是一个提供乌克兰新闻和政策分析的网站。

sentences.en: For someone, it is the history of oppression.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，这是压迫的历史。

sentences.en: For someone, it is the history of, you know, having your town being developed under the Soviet rule in the process of industrialization.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，这是在苏联统治下的工业化进程中，城镇得到发展的历史。

sentences.en: To understand all this, we should zoom out a bit.
sentences.zh: 要理解这一切，我们需要把视野放宽一点。

sentences.en: Ukraine is a country about the size of Texas that is bordered by Russia to the east and the rest of Europe to the weSt.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰是一个面积约为德克萨斯州大小的国家，东临俄罗斯，西接欧洲其他地区。

sentences.en: So it's nestled right between two superpowers, the European Union and Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以它正好坐落在两个超级大国——欧盟和俄罗斯之间。

sentences.en: A lot of people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 很多美国人

sentences.en: still refer to Ukraine as the Ukraine, like the Midwest or the South, a region.
sentences.zh: 仍然把乌克兰称为“the Ukraine”，就像称呼中西部或南部那样，把它当作一个地区。

sentences.en: It drives Ukrainians crazy.
sentences.zh: 这让乌克兰人抓狂。

sentences.en: But there is a reason for the mistake.
sentences.zh: 但这种错误是有原因的。

sentences.en: For centuries, Ukraine was a region controlled by more powerful entities around it.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，乌克兰一直是一个被周边更强大的实体所控制的地区。

sentences.en: And the word Ukraine literally means borderland.
sentences.zh: 而“乌克兰”这个词字面意思就是“边境之地”。

sentences.en: In the 1920s, much of the territory of Ukraine became part of the Soviet Union, despite the efforts of a lot of people who wanted it to be an independent country.
sentences.zh: 20世纪20年代，尽管许多希望乌克兰成为独立国家的人做出了努力，但乌克兰的大部分领土还是成为了苏联的一部分。

sentences.en: In the 1930s, millions of Ukrainians died in a famine that Stalin engineered by forcibly taking food from peasants and trapping them into starvation.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代，斯大林通过强行从农民手中夺取粮食并让他们陷入饥饿，制造了一场导致数百万乌克兰人死亡的饥荒。

sentences.en: It was the policy of collectivization.
sentences.zh: 这就是集体化政策。

sentences.en: They would take away the possessions of the people.
sentences.zh: 他们会夺走人们的财产。

sentences.en: They would collect the grain from farms and people were starving.
sentences.zh: 他们会从农场收走粮食，而人们却在挨饿。

sentences.en: Many scholars believe Stalin did this specifically to cripple the movement for Ukrainian independence.
sentences.zh: 许多学者认为，斯大林这样做正是为了削弱乌克兰的独立运动。

sentences.en: A decade later, during World War II, hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians, especially people in the east near what is now Russia, fought and died with the Soviet Red Army.
sentences.zh: 十年后，在第二次世界大战期间，成千上万的乌克兰人，特别是东部靠近现今俄罗斯地区的人们，与苏联红军并肩作战并牺牲了。

sentences.en: But a smaller number of people in the west, who wanted an independent Ukraine, allied themselves with the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 但西部的一小部分人，因为渴望一个独立的乌克兰，与纳粹结成了同盟。

sentences.en: And the Soviet Union and Germany both wanted control over Ukrainian territory.
sentences.zh: 苏联和德国都想控制乌克兰领土。

sentences.en: The territory of Ukraine was the territory of clashes during the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰领土是第二次世界大战期间冲突的中心。

sentences.en: When it was all over, even more of Ukraine was part of the USSR.
sentences.zh: 当一切结束时，乌克兰更多的领土成为了苏联的一部分。

sentences.en: Soviet authorities wanted the people of Ukraine to unite around the narrative that they had defeated the Nazis and that communism would help the country rebuild.
sentences.zh: 苏联当局希望乌克兰人民团结在“他们击败了纳粹，共产主义将帮助国家重建”这一叙事周围。

sentences.en: It was the story about winning the war and coming back victoriously and trying to rebuild the country from scratch.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于赢得战争、凯旋而归并试图从零开始重建国家的故事。

sentences.en: They had to find this inner resource to relaunch the country again.
sentences.zh: 他们必须找到这种内在资源来重新启动国家。

sentences.en: And it was very hard because they came back to empty houses, if houses at all, because mostly the territory of Ukraine was heavily bombed.
sentences.zh: 这非常困难，因为他们回到的是空房子，如果还有房子的话，因为乌克兰的领土大部分都被严重轰炸过。

sentences.en: As part of a campaign to unite Ukraine under the banner of communism, the Soviets put statues of the USSR's founding father, Vladimir Lenin, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 作为在共产主义旗帜下统一乌克兰运动的一部分，苏联人在各地都竖立了苏联开国元勋弗拉基米尔·列宁的雕像。

sentences.en: Ukraine eventually had around 5,500 statues of Lenin.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰最终拥有了大约5500座列宁雕像。

sentences.en: In the whole territory of Russia, which is 28 times the size of Ukraine, there were about 7,000 Lenins.
sentences.zh: 而在面积是乌克兰28倍的俄罗斯全境，大约有7000座列宁雕像。

sentences.en: Apart from covering Ukraine in Lenins, the Soviet Union did help develop and rebuild Ukraine in the years after World War II.
sentences.zh: 除了在乌克兰遍布列宁雕像外，苏联在二战后的几年里确实帮助开发和重建了乌克兰。

sentences.en: Small villages became big industrial cities.
sentences.zh: 小村庄变成了大型工业城市。

sentences.en: But the Soviet regime also imprisoned, by some estimates, around 2 million Ukrainians in gulags.
sentences.zh: 但苏联政权也将据估计约200万乌克兰人关进了古拉格劳改营。

sentences.en: And because the Soviet Union was not a free society, with a free press, many people had no idea that kind of repression was happening.
sentences.zh: 由于苏联不是一个拥有自由媒体的自由社会，许多人根本不知道这种压迫正在发生。

sentences.en: This whole oppression and building up labor camps and gulag in the USSR, and this information was not disclosed, so people didn't have access to that information.
sentences.zh: 这种全面的压迫、建立劳改营和古拉格，这些信息在苏联都没有被披露，所以人们无法获取这些信息。

sentences.en: The USSR said, everything is fine, as they put up more and more Lenin statues all over Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 苏联声称一切都好，同时在乌克兰各地竖立了越来越多的列宁雕像。

sentences.en: Ukraine eventually became the most Leninized territory in the USSR.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰最终成为了苏联境内“列宁化”程度最高的地区。

sentences.en: The chief state TV channel was halfway through its evening news when it got the first details of the agreement signed in Minsk.
sentences.zh: 国家电视台的主频道在播放晚间新闻时，播报了在明斯克签署的协议的初步细节。

sentences.en: Quoting from it, the anchorwoman announced, the Soviet Union no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 女主播引用协议内容宣布：苏联不复存在了。

sentences.en: In 1991, the Soviet Union collapsed.
sentences.zh: 1991年，苏联解体。

sentences.en: Ukraine became its own separate country, and so did Russia.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰成为了一个独立的国家，俄罗斯也是如此。

sentences.en: But Russia hung on to its Soviet paSt.
sentences.zh: 但俄罗斯紧紧抓住了它的苏联过去。

sentences.en: Russia, after the collapse of the USSR, officially announced that it is the successor of the USSR.
sentences.zh: 苏联解体后，俄罗斯正式宣布自己是苏联的继承国。

sentences.en: It's kind of the same.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一回事。

sentences.en: They have the music in the national anthem is the same.
sentences.zh: 他们的国歌音乐是一样的。

sentences.en: It's just the words that have changed.
sentences.zh: 只是歌词变了。

sentences.en: Russia dropped the tenets of communism and embraced capitalism in many ways.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯在许多方面放弃了共产主义原则，拥抱了资本主义。

sentences.en: But the leadership of the country, especially current President Vladimir Putin, never stopped being proud of the Soviet legacy.
sentences.zh: 但该国的领导层，特别是现任总统弗拉基米尔·普京，从未停止过对苏联遗产的自豪。

sentences.en: Ukraine, meanwhile, has struggled with its identity since gaining its independence in 1991.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，乌克兰自1991年获得独立以来，一直在身份认同问题上挣扎。

sentences.en: For a very long time, Ukraine was very indecisive, I would say, in international politics.
sentences.zh: 我想说，在很长一段时间里，乌克兰在国际政治上非常优柔寡断。

sentences.en: Would the country orient east towards Russia or west towards Europe?
sentences.zh: 这个国家是应该向东靠拢俄罗斯，还是向西靠拢欧洲？

sentences.en: It was hard for Ukraine to completely cut ties with Russia.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰很难完全切断与俄罗斯的联系。

sentences.en: For one, they relied on it for coal and gas.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们依赖俄罗斯的煤炭和天然气。

sentences.en: But also, many Ukrainians have strong cultural connections to Russia.
sentences.zh: 而且，许多乌克兰人与俄罗斯有着深厚的文化联系。

sentences.en: Ukrainians have a lot of relatives living in Russia.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人有很多亲戚住在俄罗斯。

sentences.en: It's culture, it's family, and it's business relationship, too, because both nations speak the same language.
sentences.zh: 这是文化、家庭，也是商业关系，因为两国都说同一种语言。

sentences.en: It's very easy to carry out business activities.
sentences.zh: 开展商业活动非常容易。

sentences.en: For years, the country seemed to vacillate.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这个国家似乎摇摆不定。

sentences.en: Some presidents of Ukraine leaned west towards Europe.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰的一些总统倾向于向西靠拢欧洲。

sentences.en: Others oriented east toward Russia.
sentences.zh: 另一些则向东靠拢俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And all of those Lenin statues and other communist symbols in the built environment?
sentences.zh: 那么，那些建筑环境中的列宁雕像和其他共产主义符号呢？

sentences.en: In western Ukraine, where people felt less loyalty to the Soviet era, they got rid of most of them right after independence.
sentences.zh: 在乌克兰西部，人们对苏联时代的忠诚度较低，他们在独立后不久就拆除了大部分雕像。

sentences.en: But in the rest of Ukraine, they mostly stayed put.
sentences.zh: 但在乌克兰的其他地区，它们大多保留了下来。

sentences.en: The will to remove them just wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 拆除它们的意愿根本不存在。

sentences.en: And then in 2013, the pro-Russian president, Viktor Yanukovych, tried to back out of a deal to bring Ukraine closer to joining the European Union.
sentences.zh: 然后到了2013年，亲俄总统维克多·亚努科维奇试图退出一项让乌克兰更接近加入欧盟的协议。

sentences.en: Huge protests broke out.
sentences.zh: 大规模抗议爆发了。

sentences.en: The tide had turned.
sentences.zh: 大势已去。

sentences.en: Ukrainians were in the streets saying they didn't want to be beholden to Russia anymore.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人走上街头，表示他们不想再受制于俄罗斯了。

sentences.en: These are the same protests that led to the Lenin statue being torn down in Kiev, the one that you heard at the beginning of the story.
sentences.zh: 这就是导致基辅列宁雕像被推倒的同一场抗议活动，也就是你在故事开头听到的那一幕。

sentences.en: But that's not the only statue that came down.
sentences.zh: 但那并不是唯一被推倒的雕像。

sentences.en: People started spontaneously tearing down Lenins all over Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 人们开始自发地在乌克兰各地推倒列宁雕像。

sentences.en: So much so that they had a name for it.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们为此起了一个名字。

sentences.en: Leninopad, or the falling of the Lenins.
sentences.zh: “列宁倒塌”，或者说列宁的陨落。

sentences.en: In February of 2014, following days of bloody protests in which more than 100 protesters were killed,
sentences.zh: 2014年2月，在经历了数天的血腥抗议并导致100多名抗议者死亡后，

sentences.en: Viktor Yanukovych was forced out of the presidency and fled to Russia.
sentences.zh: 维克多·亚努科维奇被迫下台并逃往俄罗斯。

sentences.en: The protesters in Ukraine established a new government.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰的抗议者成立了一个新政府。

sentences.en: It had been a violent and shocking few days for Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这对乌克兰来说是暴力且令人震惊的几天。

sentences.en: But ultimately, the protesters were victorious in their aims to topple Yanukovych and install a new government.
sentences.zh: 但最终，抗议者实现了他们的目标，推翻了亚努科维奇并组建了新政府。

sentences.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin didn't like that Ukraine was turning away from Russia and toward the European Union.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京不喜欢乌克兰背离俄罗斯转向欧盟。

sentences.en: And in March of 2014, he expressed that by taking control of a part of Ukraine called Crimea.
sentences.zh: 2014年3月，他通过控制乌克兰的一个地区——克里米亚，表达了这一点。

sentences.en: This morning, more unidentified pro-Russia armed militias controlling the streets of Crimea's capital.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，更多身份不明的亲俄武装民兵控制了克里米亚首府的街道。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, hundreds of miles to the east, Russian-backed separatists started fighting the Ukrainian military.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在数百英里外的东部，俄罗斯支持的分离主义分子开始与乌克兰军队交战。

sentences.en: By the end of 2014, Ukraine's new government, now definitively oriented towards the west, had inherited a country in crisis.
sentences.zh: 到2014年底，乌克兰的新政府已经明确转向西方，接手了一个处于危机中的国家。

sentences.en: You might think Lenin removal would be at the bottom of their liSt.
sentences.zh: 你可能认为拆除列宁雕像会是他们清单上最不重要的事情。

sentences.en: But battles with the separatists made the government want to rid its landscape once and for all of its Soviet past,
sentences.zh: 但与分离主义分子的战斗使政府想要彻底清除其景观中的苏联过去，

sentences.en: which was linked with the enemy, Russia.
sentences.zh: 因为那与敌人俄罗斯联系在一起。

sentences.en: When you have lost a certain territory, and you're likely to lose another territory on the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 当你失去了一定的领土，并且很可能在东部失去另一块领土时。

sentences.en: And you have the community that is extremely polarized, the west and eaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且你面对的是一个极度两极分化的社会，西部和东部。

sentences.en: And dismantling Lenin monuments and dismantling the Soviet past in general is a big, very, very powerful symbol.
sentences.zh: 拆除列宁纪念碑和拆除苏联过去，总的来说是一个非常、非常强大的象征。

sentences.en: One year after coming to power, the new government, led by Petro Poroshenko, decided to make the falling of the Lenins into state policy.
sentences.zh: 上台一年后，由彼得·波罗申科领导的新政府决定将“列宁倒塌”定为国家政策。

sentences.en: His allies in Ukraine's parliament passed a package of bills called decommunization laws.
sentences.zh: 他在乌克兰议会的盟友通过了一揽子被称为“去共产主义化法”的法案。

sentences.en: Various post-Soviet countries had already passed similar laws.
sentences.zh: 各种后苏联国家此前已经通过了类似的法律。

sentences.en: In Ukraine, these laws did a number of things to outlaw communism, one of which was to ban communist symbols.
sentences.zh: 在乌克兰，这些法律采取了多种手段来取缔共产主义，其中之一就是禁止共产主义符号。

sentences.en: Local authorities had a year to get rid of their Lenin statues.
sentences.zh: 地方当局有一年的时间来处理掉他们的列宁雕像。

sentences.en: If their town or streets had communist names, those had to be changed too.
sentences.zh: 如果他们的城镇或街道有共产主义名称，也必须更改。

sentences.en: Ukrainians in Kharkov have celebrated the toppling of a monument to former Soviet leader Vladimir Lenin.
sentences.zh: 哈尔科夫的乌克兰人庆祝了前苏联领导人弗拉基米尔·列宁纪念碑的倒塌。

sentences.en: A 20-meter statue of Soviet dictator Vladimir Lenin has been taken down in the Ukrainian city of Zabrasia.
sentences.zh: 一座20米高的苏联独裁者弗拉基米尔·列宁雕像在乌克兰城市扎波罗热被拆除。

sentences.en: Another day, another Lenin monument falls in Ukraine's war-torn eaSt.
sentences.zh: 又一天，又一座列宁纪念碑在乌克兰饱受战争蹂躏的东部倒塌。

sentences.en: Some places in Ukraine got really creative about complying with the decommunization laws.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰的一些地方在遵守去共产主义化法律方面非常有创意。

sentences.en: A factory in Odessa hired a sculptor to refashion the figure of Lenin as Darth Vader.
sentences.zh: 敖德萨的一家工厂雇了一位雕塑家，将列宁的形象改造成了达斯·维达。

sentences.en: Overseeing the removal of all these symbols is a government organization, the Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance.
sentences.zh: 负责监督所有这些符号拆除工作的是一个政府组织——乌克兰国家记忆研究所。

sentences.en: I'm Alina Spock.
sentences.zh: 我是阿丽娜·斯波克。

sentences.en: I'm the deputy head of Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance.
sentences.zh: 我是乌克兰国家记忆研究所的副所长。

sentences.en: Spock told me it's not easy to go from totalitarianism to democracy.
sentences.zh: 斯波克告诉我，从极权主义走向民主并不容易。

sentences.en: That's a very complicated process, definitely.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个非常复杂的过程。

sentences.en: Coming from a totalitarian society up to a democratic society.
sentences.zh: 从极权社会走向民主社会。

sentences.en: It's also not easy to erase communism from the built environment.
sentences.zh: 从建筑环境中抹去共产主义也并非易事。

sentences.en: The Soviets made things to laSt.
sentences.zh: 苏联人制造的东西是为了持久的。

sentences.en: There are long bridges lined with wrought iron hammers and sickles.
sentences.zh: 有些长桥上排列着锻铁制成的锤子和镰刀图案。

sentences.en: There are whole forests planted in such a way that if you fly over, you see the Cyrillic initials for the USSR.
sentences.zh: 还有整片森林的种植方式，让你从空中飞过时，能看到苏联的西里尔字母缩写。

sentences.en: And there are neighborhoods that do this too.
sentences.zh: 有些街区也是如此。

sentences.en: In Ternopel, for example, when we have a set of buildings which were built up in such a way so as to construct letters of USSR letters with buildings.
sentences.zh: 例如在捷尔诺波尔，我们有一些建筑群，它们的布局方式就是为了拼出苏联的字母。

sentences.en: That's one communist symbol that may have to stay for now.
sentences.zh: 那是目前可能还得保留的一个共产主义符号。

sentences.en: Spock says the process of decommunizing isn't just about removal.
sentences.zh: 斯波克说，去共产主义化的过程不仅仅是拆除。

sentences.en: It's also meant to help Ukrainians learn their own history.
sentences.zh: 它还旨在帮助乌克兰人了解他们自己的历史。

sentences.en: Which is why in many cases, the Institute of National Remembrance has suggested that towns revert to the names they had before the Soviets changed them.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在许多情况下，国家记忆研究所建议城镇恢复苏联更改之前的名称。

sentences.en: This is actually what happened to Katarina Dranova's hometown.
sentences.zh: 卡特琳娜·德拉诺娃的家乡就是这种情况。

sentences.en: The Institute of National Remembrance made a proposition to restore the historical name of the town.
sentences.zh: 国家记忆研究所提议恢复该镇的历史名称。

sentences.en: In 2016, the name of her town was restored to Komenskia.
sentences.zh: 2016年，她所在的城镇名称恢复为卡缅斯克。

sentences.en: It is rooted back to 1750 when there were Cossack settlements.
sentences.zh: 它的历史可以追溯到1750年的哥萨克定居点时期。

sentences.en: The Soviet name of Katarina's town that it had up until 2016 was Dniepro-Dzirzhensk.
sentences.zh: 卡特琳娜所在的城镇在2016年之前的苏联名称是第聂伯罗捷尔任斯克。

sentences.en: Dniepro-Dzirzhensk, and it's absolutely unpronounceable even for natives.
sentences.zh: 第聂伯罗捷尔任斯克，即使对当地人来说，这个名字也完全无法发音。

sentences.en: In Dranova's town, the majority of people just wanted to keep the old, unpronounceable Soviet name.
sentences.zh: 在德拉诺娃的家乡，大多数人只想保留那个古老且无法发音的苏联名称。

sentences.en: Because she says it was just a tiny village before the Soviets set up a metallurgical plant there.
sentences.zh: 因为她说，在苏联人在此建立冶金厂之前，这里只是一个小村庄。

sentences.en: The city owes its very existence to the Soviet history.
sentences.zh: 这座城市的存在完全归功于苏联历史。

sentences.en: It has become a town, it has become so big because of the Soviet rule.
sentences.zh: 它之所以能成为城镇，之所以能发展得如此之大，都是因为苏联的统治。

sentences.en: So it does make sense that there was a big part of the population that opposed the change.
sentences.zh: 所以，很大一部分民众反对更名是有道理的。

sentences.en: But in the end, it didn't matter if the people wanted to keep the name.
sentences.zh: 但最终，人们是否想保留这个名字并不重要。

sentences.en: Their town was named for a prominent Soviet figure, Felix Dzerzhensky, who founded the Soviet secret police.
sentences.zh: 他们的城镇是以一位著名的苏联人物——苏联秘密警察的创始人费利克斯·捷尔任斯基的名字命名的。

sentences.en: And the new law mandated the town's name be changed.
sentences.zh: 而新法律强制要求更改城镇名称。

sentences.en: What local communities do not have is the choice to keep the Soviet names.
sentences.zh: 当地社区所没有的，就是保留苏联名称的选择权。

sentences.en: That's Tarek Cyril Amar, a historian of Ukraine and Eastern Europe at Columbia University in New York.
sentences.zh: 那是塔雷克·西里尔·阿马尔，纽约哥伦比亚大学研究乌克兰和东欧的历史学家。

sentences.en: This type of, as I would say, fairly ham-fisted attempt at dealing with the Soviet legacy
sentences.zh: 这种我认为处理苏联遗产的方式相当笨拙，

sentences.en: is actually reproducing some of the Soviet legacy, some of the habits of doing things the Soviet way.
sentences.zh: 实际上是在复制部分苏联遗产，以及一些苏联式的行事习惯。

sentences.en: And this is a major criticism of the decommunization laws, that Ukraine is being kind of authoritarian about separating from their authoritarian paSt.
sentences.zh: 这也是对去共产主义化法律的主要批评，即乌克兰在与威权主义过去切割时，表现得有些威权。

sentences.en: Not just because people don't get a say in whether they change the name of their town,
sentences.zh: 不仅是因为人们在是否更改城镇名称上没有发言权，

sentences.en: but because the laws also make it illegal to join the Communist Party or display any kind of Soviet symbols,
sentences.zh: 还因为法律规定加入共产党或展示任何苏联符号都是违法的，

sentences.en: or to deny the, quote, criminal nature of the Soviet regime.
sentences.zh: 或者否认所谓的苏联政权的犯罪性质也是违法的。

sentences.en: It is forbidden to deny the criminal nature, and the criminal nature is not defined,
sentences.zh: 禁止否认其犯罪性质，但犯罪性质的定义并不明确，

sentences.en: so we're not even sure about what we're not allowed to deny or question.
sentences.zh: 所以我们甚至不确定什么是不允许否认或质疑的。

sentences.en: Scholars we spoke to for this story oppose these parts of the decommunization laws,
sentences.zh: 我们为这篇报道采访的学者反对去共产主义化法律的这些部分，

sentences.en: the ones that seem to limit freedom of speech and freedom of expression.
sentences.zh: 即那些似乎限制言论自由和表达自由的部分。

sentences.en: Dranova believes the law is too ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 德拉诺娃认为该法律过于模糊。

sentences.en: It's unclear if, for example, wearing a T-shirt with Karl Marx on it could make you criminally liable.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚，例如，穿一件印有卡尔·马克思头像的T恤是否会让你承担刑事责任。

sentences.en: Since the formal process of removing Communist symbols began in 2014,
sentences.zh: 自2014年正式开始拆除共产主义符号以来，

sentences.en: more than 50,000 objects have been renamed.
sentences.zh: 已有超过5万个对象被重新命名。

sentences.en: This includes cities, towns, villages, streets, squares, and parks.
sentences.zh: 这包括城市、城镇、村庄、街道、广场和公园。

sentences.en: And more than 2,000 monuments and memorials have been taken down or modified.
sentences.zh: 超过2000座纪念碑和纪念物被拆除或改造。

sentences.en: In general, these changes have been hardest on Ukraine's older population,
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这些变化对乌克兰的老年群体打击最大，

sentences.en: the people who lived under Soviet rule, who didn't understand how bad it was for some people.
sentences.zh: 那些生活在苏联统治下，不了解它对某些人造成了多大伤害的人。

sentences.en: Because there wasn't a free press or freedom in academia,
sentences.zh: 因为当时没有自由媒体，学术界也没有自由，

sentences.en: the extent of the repression was hidden from the general public.
sentences.zh: 压迫的程度对公众是隐瞒的。

sentences.en: Some Ukrainians are now just finding out that millions of people died because of Stalin,
sentences.zh: 一些乌克兰人现在才发现，数百万人因斯大林而死，

sentences.en: and that millions more were put into gulags.
sentences.zh: 还有数百万人被关进了古拉格集中营。

sentences.en: These notions of oppression, the facts and statistics,
sentences.zh: 这些关于压迫的概念、事实和统计数据，

sentences.en: come to them as a big revelation right now.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说现在是一个巨大的启示。

sentences.en: And there is a, you know, denial.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，还存在一种否认心理。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of change in Ukraine in the past couple of decades,
sentences.zh: 过去几十年里，乌克兰发生了巨大的变化，

sentences.en: and it's still volatile.
sentences.zh: 而且局势依然动荡。

sentences.en: Over a million people have been displaced,
sentences.zh: 超过一百万人流离失所，

sentences.en: and some eastern parts of the country are locked in semi-permanent conflict with Russia.
sentences.zh: 该国东部部分地区陷入了与俄罗斯的半永久性冲突中。

sentences.en: You live in this permanent condition of not knowing what's going to happen next and what to expect.
sentences.zh: 你生活在这种永远不知道接下来会发生什么、该期待什么的处境中。

sentences.en: That's why it is easier for someone who has been, you know,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么对于那些，你知道，

sentences.en: living under the Soviet rule to feel nostalgic about it.
sentences.zh: 生活在苏联统治下的人来说，对它产生怀旧之情更容易。

sentences.en: Dronova says that for now,
sentences.zh: 德拉诺娃说，目前，

sentences.en: many Ukrainians have shifted away from wanting to be allied with Russia
sentences.zh: 许多乌克兰人已经从希望与俄罗斯结盟，

sentences.en: and toward wanting to be allied with the EU.
sentences.zh: 转向希望与欧盟结盟。

sentences.en: But Russia still exerts a lot of political influence,
sentences.zh: 但俄罗斯仍然施加着巨大的政治影响，

sentences.en: and there are pro-Russia forces within the country that could cause trouble for a long time.
sentences.zh: 国内还有亲俄势力，可能会在很长一段时间内制造麻烦。

sentences.en: Despite feeling like some parts of the decommunization laws are too ambiguous,
sentences.zh: 尽管觉得去共产主义化法律的某些部分过于模糊，

sentences.en: Dronova thinks that removing communist symbols in public spaces
sentences.zh: 德拉诺娃认为在公共场所移除共产主义符号，

sentences.en: is an important step as Ukraine continues to develop as an independent nation.
sentences.zh: 是乌克兰作为一个独立国家继续发展的重要一步。

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我认为是这样。

sentences.en: I think it is because I think it should have been done earlier.
sentences.zh: 我认为是，因为我觉得这本应该更早完成。

sentences.en: It should be understood that it's never easy to do that.
sentences.zh: 应该明白，这样做从来都不容易。

sentences.en: There would always be a certain percent of the population who would strongly oppose that change.
sentences.zh: 总会有一定比例的人口强烈反对这种改变。

sentences.en: It's tricky for Ukraine, for any country really,
sentences.zh: 对于乌克兰，或者说对于任何国家来说，弄清楚如何抛弃压迫的象征，

sentences.en: to figure out how to leave behind symbols of oppression
sentences.zh: 同时又不完全否定和抹杀过去，都是一件棘手的事情。

sentences.en: without completely denying and erasing the paSt.
sentences.zh: 在同样曾是苏联一部分的立陶宛，

sentences.en: In Lithuania, which was also part of the USSR,
sentences.zh: 他们把许多列宁、斯大林和卡尔·马克思的雕像扔进了一个公园，

sentences.en: they threw a lot of their Lenin, Stalin, and Karl Marx statues into one park,
sentences.zh: 格鲁塔斯公园，非正式地被称为“斯大林世界”。

sentences.en: Grudis Park, unofficially called Stalin's World.
sentences.zh: 公园对游客开放。

sentences.en: And the park is open for visitors.
sentences.zh: 所以那些对整个共产主义时期和共产主义议题感到非常怀旧的人，

sentences.en: So those people who feel, you know, very sentimental about the whole communist part and communist issues,
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到那里参观，欣赏周围各种各样的列宁大雕像。

sentences.en: they are welcome to come there, visit, and enjoy the view of the big Lenin statues
sentences.zh: 乌克兰没有这样的公园，

sentences.en: in the multiple variations around.
sentences.zh: 但人们做出了一些努力来承认这些纪念物的存在和消失。

sentences.en: Ukraine doesn't have any such park,
sentences.zh: 2016年的一周里，

sentences.en: but there have been some efforts to acknowledge the existence and loss of these monuments.
sentences.zh: 一个团体获准在基辅的一个空基座周围放置了一个临时装置，

sentences.en: For a week in 2016,
sentences.zh: 那个基座曾经放置着我们在故事开头听到的被推倒的同一个列宁像。

sentences.en: a group got permission to put a temporary installation
sentences.zh: 该装置仅由金属楼梯组成，

sentences.en: around the empty pedestal in Kiev that used to hold the same Lenin we heard being toppled
sentences.zh: 人们可以走上去，站在放置在基座上方的平台上，

sentences.en: at the beginning of this story.
sentences.zh: 然后从另一侧走下来。

sentences.en: The installation consisted simply of metal stairs
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，他们可以从列宁的角度看世界，

sentences.en: that people could ascend to stand on a platform placed over the pedestal
sentences.zh: 当然，还可以自拍。

sentences.en: and then descend on the other side.
sentences.zh: 一位协助组织该装置的乌克兰策展人说，

sentences.en: In the process, they could see the world from Lenin's perspective
sentences.zh: 这是一种询问纪念碑用途的方式，

sentences.en: and, of course, take a selfie.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有自己的判断。

sentences.en: A Ukrainian curator who helped organize the installation says
sentences.zh: 这是因为，她说，

sentences.en: it's, quote,
sentences.zh: 去共产主义化首先从思想开始。

sentences.en: a way of asking what a monument is for
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由朱莉娅·巴顿和凯蒂·明格尔制作，

sentences.en: and everyone decides for themselves.
sentences.zh: 参与制作的还有谢里夫·尤萨、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德、德莱尼·霍尔、艾弗里·特鲁夫曼以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: That's because, she says,
sentences.zh: 科尔斯特是数字总监。

sentences.en: decommunization starts first in the mind.
sentences.zh: 塔琳·马扎是办公室经理。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Julia Barton and Katie Mingle
sentences.zh: 本周音乐由OK Akumi、Melodium以及我们自己的肖恩·里亚尔提供。

sentences.en: with Sharif Yusa, Emmett Fitzgerald, Delaney Hall, Avery Truffleman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢大卫·马普尔斯、亚历克斯·克莱曼诺夫、米沙·弗里德曼和卡特琳娜·德拉诺娃。

sentences.en: Kohlstedt is digital director.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW电台的一个项目，

sentences.en: Taryn Mazza is the office manager.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州美丽的奥克兰市中心的Radio Row制作。

sentences.zh: 请记住，Radiotopia将于5月8日至12日在西海岸巡演。

sentences.zh: 如果你想在旧金山见到我们，

sentences.zh: 这基本上是你买票的最后机会了。

sentences.zh: 波特兰站也快了，所以行动要快。
